notable_absence.finding: Unlike the Capella twin (cloud/eventing/eventing-overview.md), which documents a live Function configuration table (Source Bucket/Scope/Collection columns, plus the Deployed/Undeployed/Paused/Deploying/Undeploying/Pausing lifecycle-state enum), this Server overview page names no Function attribute table and no lifecycle state at all - it stays entirely at the marketing/conceptual level (what Eventing is for, how it compares to Message Queue and Polling architectures, and a use-case table by industry domain). eventing:function-lifecycle-state and the bucket/scope/collection binding surface are documented elsewhere in this batch (eventing-lifecycle.md, eventing-buckets-to-collections.md) rather than on the overview page itself.

cross_component_finding: The Server overview page names Eventing's trigger model explicitly as a 'real-time Event-Condition-Action model' - a phrase that does not appear in the Capella twin (cloud/eventing/eventing-overview.md) or elsewhere in the registry - and spends roughly half its length on head-to-head comparison tables against Message Queue and Polling architectures (dual-write problem, TCO, debug support) plus an industry-use-case table (banking, inventory, airline, healthcare, gaming, media). None of that comparative/marketing framing appears on the Capella twin, which instead leads directly with the concrete Function configuration table (bucket/scope/collection, lifecycle-state enum) that this Server page defers to other pages in the same batch. Both pages describe the same feature but are shaped for different audiences: Server's overview reads like a sales/architecture pitch aimed at someone deciding whether to adopt Eventing at all, while Capella's reads like the first page of a configuration reference for someone who already has.
